method: A rotation is built one period at a time. For each period the players are ordered by periods played so far, then by the period in which they last played (a player who has not played yet sorts first), then by player number; the first players on the field are taken and the rest are listed as resting. Because every period adds one period to the players with the lowest counts, the counts stay inside a band of at most one: if a players sit at the lower count and k are needed, taking k <= a moves k of them up and the band is unchanged, while taking k > a lifts all a and k - a of the upper count, leaving the others at the upper count, so the spread is still one. The totals are therefore floor(times k / n) and that value plus one, which is the best any rotation can do when the slots do not divide evenly; the page reports the gap in periods and minutes. Bench spells are the runs of consecutive periods a player is off the field, reported per player with the longest run. Minutes are whole periods multiplied by the period length, so a player pulled in the middle of a period is not modelled. The tie-break keeps the rotation deterministic and gives the longest rest to whoever has waited longest. The page handles 2 to 30 players, 1 to 20 periods and 1 to 120 minutes per period, does not know positions, match-ups, injuries, extra time or opponent strength, and is a planning aid, not a rulebook: competition rules on minimum playing time and re-entry override it.
